- `backend_multi_gpu_statevector` (simulation_backends): Sharded statevector training exists at development_evidence level with one measured 32-qubit complex128 forward pass on one eight-accelerator node. Production capacity expansion is not established.
- `backend_tensor_network_exact` (simulation_backends): A self-built PyTorch tensor-network path exists without a cuTensorNet-class contraction planner, so the exact regime is narrower than the CUDA-Q baseline.
- `backend_density_matrix` (simulation_backends): FlagQuantum executes a program as an exact dense density matrix through the registered density_matrix_execution entry, which records the owner, the limitation set, and the focused suite behind the engine and its mode selection. The row stays partial because the engine covers less than the CUDA-Q backend: the circuit IR carries no mid-circuit measurement, reset, or classically conditioned instruction, so this route cannot express them, and the path takes no accelerator.
- `backend_stim_stabilizer` (simulation_backends): All three questions the row names are now answered over the representation. The representation half is closed: a Stim-backed Clifford sampling engine samples a thousand-wire GHZ chain, so the wire counts a dense amplitude store cannot hold are reachable, and Stim is Apache-2.0 licensed and independent of every NVIDIA component, which is why this was integration rather than research. The execution half landed as an execution mode: `plan` and `run` reach the engine through `state_mode='stabilizer'`, report a plan, a result, and execution evidence, and route lowered expectation requests as well as sampling ones, so `fq.expectation` is answered exactly over the tableau without a shot count. The noisy half landed last, and it is what closes the first of the two narrowings this row used to record: the routed mode admits a program carrying noise instructions, lowering a scene-level `NoiseModel` into positioned channel instructions the way the density-matrix route does, and the engine draws the frames a channel defines at the instruction the caller put it at. Which of the engine's two sampling entry points applies is read from the program rather than passed alongside it, so an inline channel and an equivalent model reach the same route and one plan replays to one drawing. That route is sampling-only for a noisy program and refuses an exact value by name, because a frame draw answers outcomes rather than one Pauli; a channel whose Kraus operators are not a mixture of Pauli frames is refused while planning, out of the engine's own survey, before a plan is published. The detector error model is connected to the same engine through `flagquantum.qec.sample_memory_circuit`, which lowers a memory circuit once and reads detection events and observable flips off the recorded bits, but that entry point takes a `MemoryCircuit` and a phenomenological noise record rather than reaching the engine from an ordinary run. The exact readout itself needs no external engine, so it survives the representation being unavailable.
- `backend_dynamics` (simulation_backends): FlagQuantum has a real Lindblad engine with RK4 integration, validation codes, and evidence fields, so this capability is not missing. Three walls separate it from the baseline: CPU-only hard rejection, a dense four-to-the-n Hamiltonian with a fixed step, and a static Hamiltonian. Batching and gradients are rejected.
- `kraus_channel_algebra` (noise_and_error_models): A general Kraus constructor exists and is validated. `KrausChannel` accepts an arbitrary operator list, refuses a set that is not trace-preserving (completeness compared at `atol = rtol = 1e-6`) and a dimension that is not a positive power of two, serializes through the `flagquantum.kraus_channel.v1` schema, and reaches simulation through `NoiseModel.add` and `Circuit.noisy_density_matrix`. What is absent is the operator type the CUDA-Q surface builds a channel from: no matrix-valued operator participates in operator algebra, which is the gap `matrix_and_custom_operator` already records.
- `detector_error_model` (noise_and_error_models): Both directions of the stim text interchange work. `from_memory_circuit` builds a model exactly for Pauli noise over the reference Clifford gate set; `to_stim_text` emits text stim 1.16.0 parses; `from_stim_text` reads everything stim wrote in a 240-model developer-time sweep except a `repeat` block, and `str(model.flattened())` is a complete route around that one refusal; both readings of a `^` separator are offered under upstream's own `use_decomp_suggestions` flag name, and the default is the one stim itself means, measured against stim's own sampler rather than asserted. The model can also state that mechanisms are alternatives rather than independent, which is the one thing its parity matrices cannot carry: an error id groups them, the marginal rates and the sampler read a group as one fault, and the text writer refuses an id-carrying model instead of printing an independent one under the same probabilities. The row stays partial because conversion is narrower than the baseline at the input end: `from_memory_circuit` accepts one circuit record and one noise record, so an arbitrary circuit carrying detector and observable annotations has no route to a model, and a non-Pauli channel is refused rather than decomposed. The output end is no longer one of the limits: `circuit_from_detector_error_model` writes a model as the detector-level realization it already is and `detector_error_model_from_circuit` reads it back exactly, error ids included, so a model reaches the stabilizer engine without a statevector and without a second construction. What that route does not and cannot return is the circuit the model was built from, because a model states which detector parities a fault flips and never which measurements compose a detector; it returns the canonical detector-level circuit every model determines, with the detector count stated by the caller. `flagquantum/qec/IMPLEMENTATION.md` records the sweeps, the arithmetic and the realization. The audit confirmed this absence and now cites the refusal that states it: `flagquantum/qec/dem_circuit.py:199` reads a circuit back into the model it realizes, but only for a circuit `circuit_from_detector_error_model` built, and `:209` gives the reason in its own words -- it states what a realization is rather than guessing at what an arbitrary annotated circuit might mean. The reader's preconditions are the shape of the absence: every instruction a fault frame or a measurement, measurements one per wire in wire order and after every frame, and every wire a frame names flipped by one of its branches. An annotated circuit from elsewhere satisfies none of them and is refused rather than interpreted.
- `spin_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): The earlier reason overstated the gap and is replaced by measurement. Products, sums, and scalars are not absent: Observable in flagquantum/observables/__init__.py implements __add__, __sub__, __mul__, __rmul__, __neg__, and __matmul__, and each returns an Observable rather than a matrix, so X(0) + Z(0) is an Observable carrying two terms and 2 * X(0), X(0) * 2, X(0) - Z(0), X(0) @ Y(1), and -X(0) are all Observables. What is genuinely absent on the Pauli side is four operations: commutator, anticommutator, exponential together with its exp spelling, and __pow__. Each of the first three raises AttributeError and X(0) ** 2 raises TypeError, so no commutator and no exponential of a Pauli sum can be taken. The same package already gives the fermionic and bosonic siblings their commutators, FermionOperator.commutator and FermionOperator.anticommutator in flagquantum/observables/fermion.py and BosonOperator.commutator and BosonOperator.anticommutator in flagquantum/observables/boson.py, so the gap is a Pauli-side asymmetry rather than an absent algebra. Observable also exposes no dense or matrix accessor, so a caller who needs the matrix of a Pauli sum reaches PauliSum.dense or the simulation route instead. All four missing operations are additive members of Observable, which is one of the 36 names in the Stable Core export set, so closing this row is an API change under rule 8 with no approval today, and the row stays partial rather than partially built.
- `super_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): The algebra is implemented: `flagquantum/operators/superoperator.py` states a superoperator as a sum of `coefficient * left @ state @ right` terms, where a missing side is a one-sided multiplication, with the three CUDA-Q constructors and an accumulating `+=`; `apply` and `dense` are two independent formulas in the repository-wide row-major vectorization `vec(A rho B) = (A (x) B^T) vec(rho)`, and the Lindblad generator assembled that way is the same arithmetic as `Liouvillian.dense()`, so the check that used to read 4.441e-16 now reads exactly 0.0. `SuperOperator.adjoint()` returns the Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint as a term-list transform -- conjugate the coefficient, adjoint each factor on the side it already occupied -- and it satisfies both `<sigma, L rho> = <L^dag sigma, rho>` to 1.2e-15 and `adjoint().dense() == dense().conj().T` to 2.0e-15 against an oracle built from the action, so `Liouvillian` derives its reverse map from it instead of assembling a second one. The factor contract has two implementations, `torch.Tensor` and `PauliSum`, both supplying `__matmul__`, `__rmatmul__` and `dense()`, and `PauliSum.adjoint()` keeps the matrix-free path matrix-free, so a matrix-free Hamiltonian enters a term and is reversed without being materialized. The two representation directions are read by one coordinate transform rather than by two pieces of arithmetic. `from_kraus` turns a Kraus list into a term list -- one two-sided term per operator, coefficient one -- so a channel enters the algebra instead of standing beside it, and `terms` returns each `(coefficient, left, right)`, which is the per-term accessor the row used to report as absent. `matrix_in_basis` reads the map in any orthonormal basis of matrices as `P^dag dense() P`, where column `i` of `P` is `vec(B_i)`, so the Pauli transfer matrix is that transform in `normalized_pauli_basis(n)`, which `flagquantum/simulation/pauli.py` owns and which is `P_i / sqrt(d)` in `pauli_words(n)` order with the identity at index zero. Both properties of the basis are checked rather than assumed, because dropping either returns a different quantity under the same name: `d**2` entries, so the matrix is the map and not its projection onto a subspace, and `trace(B_i^dag B_j) == delta_ij` to eight epsilons of the map dtype, so `P^dag` is `P^-1` and the product is the similarity transform rather than the Gram-corrected `P^dag D P`. A basis that is empty, the wrong length, not a `(d, d)` tensor of the map dtype, spread across two devices, off the CPU, or unnormalized is refused by name. Measured against an oracle built from the map's own `apply`, the transform agrees to 2.220e-16 at one wire and to 6.661e-16 on a two-qubit depolarizing channel's 16 x 16 map, and exactly 0.0 for the two-wire identity; a bit flip reads `diag(1, 1, 1 - 2p, 1 - 2p)` to 6.999e-08 over p in {0.1, 0.25, 0.4} and amplitude damping reads its analytic transfer matrix to 1.206e-08 in the channel's default precision, against 1.192e-08 for the same channels built with complex128 Kraus -- residuals set by the probability being quantized to single precision before the square root, since `sqrt(p)` at p = 0.4 is 0.6324555367458368 against 0.6324555320336759, rather than by the transform. The identity row `(1, 0, ..., 0)`, which is trace preservation in this basis, holds to 6.999e-08 over five default-precision channels and to 2.220e-16 with complex128 Kraus, while amplitude damping's identity *column*, which is unitality, differs from it by exactly gamma = 3.000e-01 -- so the two statements are distinguishable here rather than conflated. `flagquantum/algorithms/pec.py` now reads its quasi-probability decomposition through this pair instead of carrying a second transfer-matrix implementation, so the matrix the PEC unit inverts and the matrix this algebra produces are one object seen in two modules. The Choi half of the remaining transforms is implemented. `choi()` reads the same map in a third index order, `J[(a, i), (b, j)] = E(E_ab)[i, j]`, by regrouping the four indices `(i, j, a, b)` of `dense()` into `(a, i, b, j)`, and it is pinned against `sum_ab E_ab (x) E(E_ab)` built from the map's own `apply` at exactly 0.000e+00 on every fixture in both dtypes, so the transform is the definition rather than a second transcription of one. The convention is pinned where the candidates are distinguishable rather than where they coincide: at one wire two of the three competing index orders return the same matrix, and at three levels all three are separated by 3.750e-02, 7.000e-01 and 3.750e-02 on a depolarizing channel, which is what the test asserts against. `trace(choi())` equals `trace(E(I))` to 0.000e+00 on the identity map, a depolarizing channel, amplitude damping at gamma = 0.4, and the transpose map, so a trace-preserving map's Choi matrix has trace `d`; that is a property of the map and not of the convention, and it holds for the transpose map, which is why it cannot separate complete positivity from mere positivity. `is_completely_positive()` is the certificate that does: it reads the smallest eigenvalue of the Choi matrix's Hermitian part, returns `True` for the identity, a rank-deficient dephasing channel, a three-Kraus depolarizing channel and a single scaled operator in both dtypes, and `False` for the transpose map, whose smallest Choi eigenvalue is exactly -1.000000 against a Choi scale of exactly 1.000000 at two and at three levels. Its tolerance is relative to the Choi matrix's own spectral scale because an absolute one is measurably wrong: over a rotated rank-deficient dephasing channel rescaled by `c`, whose smallest Choi eigenvalue is exactly zero in exact arithmetic, the absolute deviation reaches 1.337e+06 epsilons at `c = 1024` and four levels in complex64 and 9.956e+05 in complex128, while the ratio to the Choi scale stays constant across the whole five-decade sweep to better than 1e-9 -- 1.275668 in complex64 and 0.949502 in complex128 -- and an absolute threshold of eight epsilons would have refused that channel from `c = 4` onward, where the measured absolute deviation is already 20.411 epsilons in complex64 and 15.192 in complex128. A map whose Choi matrix is not Hermitian is refused by name rather than answered `False`, because complete positivity is a property of maps that take Hermitian states to Hermitian states and a generator is not one: left-multiplying by an anti-Hermitian matrix is measured 1.000e+00 away from Hermitian at a Choi scale of 1.000e+00. Both normalization conditions are read off the same matrix rather than re-derived -- the first partial trace of the Choi matrix is `E(I)`, so a unital map has the identity there, and the second is the identity exactly for a trace-preserving map, both measured at 0.000e+00 against the map's own action and separated by amplitude damping, whose first partial trace is `diag(1 + gamma, 1, ..., 1 - gamma)`. That read-off is a public accessor rather than a recomputation: `SuperOperator.partial_trace(register, *, max_bytes=...)` sums one of the two registers of the Choi index order and returns the `(d, d)` matrix of the other, `input` for `E(I)` and `output` for `trace(E(E_ab))` indexed by the input labels, so the caller who wanted either normalization no longer reaches for `apply` and `einsum`. It is checked against an oracle built from the map's own `apply` -- `E(I)` in one call and one call per matrix unit for the other register -- rather than against a second reshape of `choi()`, so agreement is a statement about the Choi index order instead of a transcription of it, and the fixtures separate the two registers rather than hiding a swap behind a map that is both unital and trace preserving: a one-sided action is neither, so its two traces differ by 1.281e+00 at three levels and neither is the identity. The byte ceiling is `choi()`'s, inherited rather than re-derived, because the trace is read off that matrix, and a `register` that is neither value is refused by name with the two that are. The accessor is additive scope beyond the surface the approved W6-02a proposal enumerated: that proposal listed the CUDA-Q constructors, `apply`, a byte-ceilinged `dense`, scalar multiplication, `__add__` and `__eq__` and named partial trace as outside it, and the repository owner authorized this accessor as additive work, which is why it carries no proposal of its own -- `SuperOperator` is not a stable export and appears in neither API baseline, so no frozen contract moves and no rule 8 authorization is involved. `kraus()` is the other direction, and it is a read-off rather than a fit: the Choi matrix of a completely positive map is `sum_k |v_k><v_k|` scaled by its eigenvalues, so the eigenvectors of `choi()` unstacked back into `d` x `d` matrices are the operators, each weighted by the square root of its eigenvalue, at most `d**2` of them and in descending weight. The two numbers the reconstruction could get wrong are measured where they are distinguishable rather than assumed. The unstacking index order is checked where a transposed reading is a *different map*: dropping the transpose on amplitude damping at gamma = 0.4 is measured 2.625e-01 away from the map's own action, 4.000e-01 away in the dense form, and exactly -2.625282042778918e-01 in the `[0, 0]` entry, which is `-gamma * rho[1, 1]` to the last digit, while this form agrees to 5.594e-17. The count is the Choi rank rather than the length of any list that was supplied, so a unitary channel returns one operator and three operators spanning two dimensions return two, checked at two, three and four levels, and the weights are the spectrum, so the squared Frobenius norm of each returned operator is its Choi eigenvalue. The list is a Kraus representation and not a canonical one -- the eigenvector phases, and any mixing inside a degenerate eigenvalue, are the eigenproblem's rather than this method's -- so what is pinned is the count, the weights and the map. Reconstructing through `from_kraus` returns the map it came from: the action agrees to 5.594e-17 at two levels and 1.665e-16 at three, and the dense form to 1.110e-16 and 4.441e-16 in complex128, with the worst deviation over every fixture and both dtypes at 1.788e-07 in complex64, which is the dtype's own rounding rather than the decomposition's. The refusals are the same question `is_completely_positive` asks, answered with a different consequence: a map whose Choi matrix has a negative eigenvalue is refused by name with that eigenvalue and the tolerance, because no Kraus list denotes it and returning the closest one would substitute a different map silently -- the transpose map's smallest Choi eigenvalue is exactly -1.000000 against a scale of exactly 1.000000 at two and at three levels -- and a map that does not preserve Hermiticity is refused with the certificate's own sentence, measured 1.000e+00 away from Hermitian. The byte ceiling is `choi()`'s again and is inherited rather than re-derived, so a four-level map is answered under the default ceiling and refused above a 16-byte one with `choi()`'s own message. The tolerance is not a second one either: the eigenproblem and the tolerance rule live in one private helper both methods call, because two copies of the rule would disagree exactly on the rank-deficient channels the rule exists for. The row stays partial rather than supported because CUDA-Q exposes neither transform, so this accessor is additive scope rather than a gap against it, and because no registry entry covers the algebra itself -- its only `maturity_ref` is the Lindblad route that consumes it. Still absent, on its own evidence: no application of a map to a subsystem, since `partial_trace` reads a register of the Choi matrix rather than acting on part of a state. That absence is additive scope in the same sense as the rest of this row rather than a gap against CUDA-Q, which exposes no such operation either, and it is recorded here so the row's remaining distance is named rather than silent. The audit read the last clause against the whole tree rather than against this class, because the operation it calls absent does exist for two other representations. `flagquantum/simulation/density_matrix.py` exports `apply_unitary_density(rho, matrix, wires, n_wires)` and `apply_kraus_density(rho, kraus, wires, n_wires)`, and both expand the local operator onto the named wires of a state with `expand_operator` before acting, which is an application to a subsystem. So the absence this row records is the object-valued route and not the operation: `SuperOperator` carries 15 public members -- `adjoint`, `apply`, `choi`, `dense`, `dimension`, `dtype`, `from_kraus`, `is_completely_positive`, `kraus`, `left_multiply`, `left_right_multiply`, `matrix_in_basis`, `partial_trace`, `right_multiply`, `terms` -- and every one of them either builds the map, reads the map, or acts on a whole state, while the two functions above take a raw matrix and a `KrausChannel` instead. `from_kraus` is the bridge between those two worlds, so a caller holding a `SuperOperator` still has to name the operators and the wires again rather than pass the map. `apply_local` occurs 24 times under `flagquantum/` and every occurrence is a runtime execution kernel applying a local *gate* inside an executor, which is neither an operator nor a channel and is why none of them is a counterexample.
- `chemistry_domain_library` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): All three parts of the row now exist and the row is still narrower than the baseline. The ansatz is `flagquantum/algorithms/chemistry.py`, which enumerates the single and double excitations of an electron count in a spin-orbital count, builds the fermionic generator of one, emits the exact circuit that realizes its exponential, composes them into the UCCSD circuit, and covers a hardware-efficient and a coupler hardware-efficient ansatz with a parameter count; the gate sequences are the ones CUDA-Q's own kernels apply, so a workload built around them transfers. The driver this row names first is the other two parts, and it is where this repository departs from the baseline. `flagquantum/algorithms/chemistry_integrals.py` evaluates the one- and two-electron integrals of a molecule itself, by McMurchie-Davidson recursion over contracted Cartesian Gaussians, and `flagquantum/algorithms/molecular.py` solves restricted closed-shell Hartree-Fock from the bare core Hamiltonian, transforms the integrals into the molecular-orbital basis, folds a frozen core and restricts to an active space where one is asked for, and returns the Jordan-Wigner observable beside the Hartree-Fock energy and, at or below 1024 determinants, the exact S_z = 0 ground-state energy. The Boys function and its recursion are the numerically delicate part of that. The baseline reaches the same entry point through PySCF, and CUDA-Q's own C++ molecule type resolves the driver string through a package registry and ignores it, so the driver name is not a selection there either. This repository binds no chemistry package at all: the numbers are produced here, in double precision, by torch alone, which is what makes this row's evidence reproducible inside this checkout rather than dependent on an external numerical library's version. Three registry entries carry the row, one per part it names, because the parts have separate entry points and separate failure boundaries: the engine is a numerical kernel, the driver is the entry point a user calls, and the ansatz is state preparation. What is still narrower than the baseline is in `baseline_gap` rather than hidden. Beyond it, refusals are deliberate and stated rather than silent: an element outside H through Ne, a basis name other than sto-3g, a multiplicity other than one, an odd electron count, and an active electron count whose parity differs from the total's are each refused instead of being given a contraction, a substitution, or a solution of the wrong symmetry; an occupied index above a virtual one is refused by the ansatz rather than emitting an empty ladder that would be a local rotation rather than an excitation. One divergence in the ansatz part remains: `uccsd_excitations` fills the lowest n_electrons spin orbitals where CUDA-Q's `get_uccsd_excitations` divides by two before rounding up, so the two agree on even electron counts only. The audit measured every clause of that token rather than the first. No chemistry package is bound: pyscf, openfermion and openfermion-pyscf occur in neither pyproject.toml nor dependency-policy.toml. One basis and ten elements are read off module constants rather than off prose -- `BASIS_SETS` in flagquantum/algorithms/chemistry_integrals.py is the one-tuple ('sto-3g',) and `ATOMIC_NUMBERS` runs H through Ne -- so `molecular.py`'s STO-3G default is the only value the table can accept rather than a default a caller may change. Open-shell is refused by name and not merely unsupported: the electron-count check raises naming the unrestricted and restricted-open-shell solves the module does not have. Non-singlet, symmetry tapering, analytic nuclear gradient and geometry optimisation have no implementation and no constant; point-group symmetry occurs twice in the package and both occurrences are docstring sentences declaring its absence.
- `execution_entry_points` (algorithm_layer): The earlier reason was half false and is replaced by measurement. translate has an equivalent: flagquantum/compiler/translate.py exports translate(program, format=...) and TRANSLATION_FORMATS is the four names openqasm-2.0, openqasm-3.0, qcis-1.0, and qir-2.0, read from target_emission.EMISSION_PROFILES rather than declared a second time, and an unaccepted spelling such as qir:0.1 is refused by name. draw exists too, as flagquantum.drawer.draw(program, format=text) alongside draw_text, draw_mpl, to_drawable_circuit, and the drawer styles, which is narrower than the CUDA-Q surface rather than absent. What is genuinely absent is evolve: no public entry point evolves a state under a time-dependent schedule. The dynamics surface exists as flagquantum.lindblad and flagquantum.simulation's evolve_density_matrix, and the reason it stays out of this row is that the integrators accept a constant generator with no time argument, which is what API_CHANGE_PROPOSAL_065 asks to change. The shared limit is reachability rather than implementation: run, counts, probabilities, samples, expectation, compile, plan, gradient, train, twin, submit, and restore_job are the only entry points among the 36 root exports, so draw and translate are reached by their own module path and neither the drawing nor the dynamics surface is part of the root contract. The audit re-read the accessor clause and found a second name in the tree containing the word: `flagquantum/simulation/density_matrix.py` exports `apply_unitary_density(rho, matrix, wires, n_wires)`, which takes a unitary as an argument and acts with it, so it consumes a unitary rather than reading one out and is not an accessor. The one accessor is `get_unitary` at `flagquantum/simulation/unitary.py:67`, whose module `__all__` is the pair `MAX_UNITARY_WIRES` and `get_unitary`, and `flagquantum.simulation.__all__` re-exports it -- so it is reachable from the root package as `flagquantum.simulation.get_unitary` and not as `flagquantum.get_unitary`, which is the distinction the token now spells out. `apply_unitary_density` is absent from `flagquantum.simulation`'s `__all__` as well, so the two names do not sit at the same level.
- `error_mitigation` (algorithm_layer): Zero-noise extrapolation, probabilistic error cancellation and Clifford data regression. An observable is measured at several error strengths by scaling the one error-probability parameter each noise channel declares, and the curve is continued to zero by polynomial least squares or Richardson extrapolation, which reports the residual it left and the variance amplification of its weights. The channel families whose parameters are not error probabilities are refused by name, and a model that declares a readout rule is refused rather than measured without it, because the estimate is Tr(O rho) and classical readout confusion is applied after measurement. Beside that, a channel the model declares as a Pauli channel is inverted exactly by decomposing its inverse into a signed combination of Pauli words read off its Pauli transfer matrix, one location at a time, which reports the sampling overhead gamma squared that a sampled implementation would pay and refuses by measured magnitude the channel families whose transfer matrix is not diagonal and the channels whose transfer eigenvalue reaches zero. The third member landed as flagquantum.algorithms.cdr: each phase, rx, ry, rz and u1 rotation of the target is snapped to its nearest quarter turn and rewritten into the named Clifford word for that turn, those training circuits' ideal values are read from exact density simulation and their noisy values from the same simulation of the declared model, and the affine relation between the two is fitted and applied to the target. Every training circuit is accepted by flagquantum.simulation.stabilizer.require_clifford_program before it is measured, so the membership that would make the training set cheap on hardware is enforced and never exploited: this path pays the target's own simulation cost and claims no capacity advantage from it, and it says so where the estimate is. A model that names an operation the rewrite removes is refused, because the model keys its channels on gate names and every training point would otherwise receive less noise than the target, and a program that declares a measurement or observable request is refused because the path reads Tr(O rho) and consumes no request. The fit's largest residual is the only diagnostic of the affine premise and is reported as absent rather than as an arithmetic zero when no degree of freedom was left, so a two-point fit's agreement is an identity rather than a check. The fourth member landed as flagquantum.algorithms.readout_mitigation, the leg the other three named as absent: the readout rules a NoiseModel declares are grouped into disjoint blocks, one block per rule, and each block's transpose inverse is applied to a measured distribution. The transposition is the index convention rather than a detail -- a calibration table is written with the true outcome as its row index while the vector the forward path produces has qubit 0 as its most significant bit -- and the two inverses differ by 0.14285714 in the maximum entry on ((0.9, 0.1), (0.2, 0.8)) and agree on a symmetric table, so the relation is asserted directly. A rule naming several qubits is inverted as one block because its marginals are a different operator, a qubit named by two rules is refused rather than confused twice, and a block whose smallest singular value reaches the declared floor is refused by measured magnitude rather than inverted into weights no shot count can support. The amplification the correction costs is the whole map's induced 1-norm, which for a map that is a tensor product of disjoint blocks is the product of the blocks' own rather than the worst block's, and the standard error a shot-based estimate inherits is that amplification over the square root of the count. The corrected vector is not forced onto the simplex: its negative mass is summed and reported beside it rather than clipped, because clipping would return a different vector under the same name. The fifth member landed as flagquantum.algorithms.folding, which reaches the scaled-noise curve without naming a channel parameter at all: the program is lengthened by an exact identity -- each instruction followed by its own inverse and then the instruction again, distributed one instruction at a time or as whole repeated bodies -- so the noise its instructions carry runs more times while nothing but the dtype's rounding changes what is computed, measured at 1.6e-16 on the five-instruction body h, cx, rz, ry, t at complex128 under both strategies. It is a different unit of scale rather than another scaling: what it reports is the length ratio it realized, that ratio is the abscissa the extrapolation fits against rather than the factor requested, and a call naming both a fold and a scaling callable is refused because the product of a length ratio and a channel parameter names neither. Two consequences are recorded rather than hidden. The circuit strategy repeats whole bodies so its realized ratio is 1 + 2m and a request of 1.4 is met by 3.0, while the gate strategy meets that same request exactly in seven instructions and meets 2.2 exactly in eleven where the circuit strategy's next reachable ratio, 3.0, costs it fifteen; and because both reach a ratio in steps of two instructions, two distinct requests can realize one length -- 1.4 and 2.6 both realize 3.0 on a body of five -- which is refused by naming the duplicated ratio rather than by failing inside the solve, since repeated abscissas make the linear system singular. A gate fold spends its pairs leftmost first, so a readout blind to where they land reads a flat curve over a program whose noise genuinely grew: with depolarizing at 0.03 on all five gates the added pair lands on the leading h and zz(0, 1) reads 0.672956129888 at both ratio 1.0 and ratio 1.4 while xx(0, 1) reads 0.242863810368 and 0.223823288052. The fold needs no noise model, which is what lets it run where a channel-scaling run is refused, but what it assumes instead -- that repeating an instruction repeats that instruction's error and changes no other instruction's error -- is a statement about crosstalk and drift that no program carries and no measurement here checks. What the family still does not carry: a tensored or sparse approximation for a block wider than the ceiling, any correction of a confusion the model does not declare, and any estimate of the noise a fold amplifies.
- `variational_algorithms` (algorithm_layer): Both halves of the baseline's solver library are registered capabilities now, and the two entries are separate because their premises and their readings differ. The QAOA half landed as flagquantum.algorithms.variational and is registered as algorithms_variational_solvers: a weighted MaxCut edge list is checked once and reaches both the cost layer the ansatz applies and the operator the energy is scored against through the same tuple, which is the agreement the primitives beside it did not carry -- qaoa_circuit took edges and qaoa_loss took a Hamiltonian, and nothing related the two, so a caller could score one graph's ansatz against another graph's operator and read a number about a problem nobody posed. The operator is sum over edges of w_ij Z_i Z_j, whose value on a basis state is the edge total less twice the cut, and the entry point refuses a self-loop, a repeated undirected pair, a non-finite or non-real weight and an empty edge list by naming what a cost layer would have mishandled. The uniform superposition is an eigenstate of every cost and mixer term, so the gradient at a zero start is exactly zero at every layer count, which is why the start is a required argument rather than a default; a finite layer count is an approximation, so the energy is an expectation rather than a bound; and the fitted angles, the energy and the trajectory are all the result carries, with sampling, decoding and ranking left to the caller. The VQE half is the four entry points flagquantum.algorithms.core.run_vqe, run_adapt_vqe, run_hybrid_vqe and run_layerwise_vqe, which the examples, the services layer and the benchmarks already call. They are implemented and exercised -- tests/unit/test_vqe_optimizer_factory.py holds their optimizer-factory contract and tests/test_algorithms.py and tests/test_hybrid_optimization.py drive them on circuits -- and they are now a registered capability of their own, algorithms_vqe_solvers, with tests/unit/test_vqe_solvers.py as its focused unit and examples/algorithms/vqe_solvers.py as its golden path; that registration closed the first of the two things that kept this row partial. It did not close the second, the surface shape, and this row still does not claim the baseline's shape. The registration also settled two readings a caller could get wrong, recorded here because this row's evidence is what a reader reaches first. The ADAPT screen differentiates the objective at the appended angle and is therefore exact, so a reference state that is an eigenstate of every pool generator screens every direction to exactly zero, selects nothing and reports converged=True while above the ground energy: measured on two qubits against ZZ - X0 - X1, whose ground energy is -2.2360679774997898, the pool (ry, rz, rx) on wire 0 selects index 0 at a screened gradient of -1.0 from the |00> state and selects nothing from the |++> state. And converged reports why the loop stopped rather than how close the energy came, so a pool of one with a zero tolerance reports True at -1.4142135623730354 and a tolerance exit reports True at -1.4142135623730951, while a run that spent its iteration budget reports False at 0.999999999 -- which is the run furthest from the ground energy, so the flag is an exit test in neither direction. Both readings were previously reachable only by reading the loop, and one of them was reachable only as a torch backward error: a builder that supplies no gradient, or a pool element that adds no dependence at the appended angle, now raises ValueError naming the entry point and the cause instead of RuntimeError: element 0 of tensors does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn. The other is the shape difference the baseline names: the CUDA-Q baseline offers a solver object whose ansatz and optimizer are configuration, and this package offers entry points whose ansatz is a circuit builder the caller supplies, so the two surfaces are not one-to-one even where the mathematics matches. Still absent, each on its own evidence: a solver object carrying a pluggable ansatz registry, any constraint, penalty or slack term, adaptive and multi-angle QAOA variants, a warm start from a classical heuristic, a chemistry front end, and the constrained derivative-free handling that COBYLA gives the baseline's VQE path and that this package's SPSA and Nelder-Mead units do not provide. One absence this row used to name is closed and is corrected here rather than left standing: a cost Hamiltonian for a general QUBO or Ising instance is not missing, because flagquantum.algorithms.qubo already carries qubo_to_ising, ising_to_qubo and max_cut_qubo. One of those absences narrowed without the row moving: the gradient-free route within the QAOA half now exists at the objective level rather than the optimizer level. maxcut_objective returns the very callable run_qaoa minimizes, checked through the same edge list and split into gammas and betas the same way, and it is readable with float() without a backward pass, so SPSAOptimizer and NelderMeadOptimizer -- both already shipped and previously reachable from no solver entry point -- can be handed it. Measured on the one-layer triangle from a flat 0.05 start against the -1.0 optimum, Adam reaches -0.9999997615814209 in 300 steps, SPSA -0.9999911189079285 in 400 steps at 1201 evaluations, and Nelder-Mead -1.0000003576278687 in 706 evaluations; the simplex reaches the optimum while reporting converged=False, because that flag measures the simplex collapsing and not the energy arriving, and the route is asserted on the energy rather than on the flag. It is deliberately not a second optimizer parameter on run_qaoa: an SPSA step is a rate-limited update from two objective values while a simplex is a whole run released at once, so one parameter could not carry both shapes without a dispatch hiding which method ran. What the route is not is a constrained method or a sampled one, so the COBYLA gap, every constraint, penalty and slack term, and the shot-based path all remain absent, and the row stays partial.
- `qec_code_library` (quantum_error_correction): The repetition code, the rotated surface code and the Steane code are declared as code records and each produces a memory-experiment source with detector and observable layouts, so a distance-d rotated patch is expressible and a code carrying both a Z-type and an X-type readout is expressible through Steane. A code record can also be read into matrices rather than only into a circuit: css_code_matrices lifts its four blocks into a CssCodeMatrices record, which carries hz, hx, lz and lx together, so a code whose stabilizers are known reaches a code-capacity detector error model on either readout basis without a gadget being built for it and without losing a fault family. The other direction has since landed as well: CssCode takes hz, hx, lz and lx that a caller writes and returns the same kind of record the three declared families return, so a family this package does not declare now has a route in. That route checks rather than assumes -- the two check families commute, a declared logical operator commutes with the opposite check family while not lying in the span of its own, the declared operators of a family pair up non-degenerately, and the shared width leaves at least one logical qubit -- and it computes the distance by searching the code instead of reading it off the operator the caller wrote down, so the same Steane code reports three whether its logical operator is written at weight three or at weight seven. What that search does not do is run without a bound, and the bound is the caller's to accept. One limit survives from the declared records, because it is the protocol's rather than this route's: a logical observable that is neither pure X nor pure Z is refused rather than half-read. The other one is gone, and the way it went is the round's finding. A check used to be required to be pure, on the record's own claim that a mixture would need a second ancilla and a second CNOT direction. Half of that claim was wrong: the second CNOT direction is needed and the second ancilla is not, because the X-factor pairs are controlled by the declared ancilla and the Z-factor pairs control it, so one ancilla measures the product of the two. flagquantum.qec.CodeCheck therefore states one coupling order -- the Z-factor pairs first, each reading a data wire into the ancilla, then the X-factor pairs, each reading the ancilla out into a data wire -- and the boundary between the two runs is exactly what the emitted H pair wraps. A pure check is the case whose second run is empty, so the two emission shapes are one rule and the pure checks' source is byte-identical across the change. flagquantum.qec.ZxxzSurfaceCode is the first record built on it. The colour family has since landed as a record of its own, and it is the first record here whose matrices are derived rather than transcribed: triangular_colour_code builds the three-face-colourable triangular patch from its distance alone and returns the same CssCode record, so a caller no longer writes six-vertex faces out as rows. Two properties of it are asserted rather than implied. Its two check families are literally one matrix, because every face carries one X-type and one Z-type stabilizer, so the patch is self-dual and the both-basis route is exercised without a second table being kept in step. And its checks are not all of one weight -- a face on the patch's edge spans four qubits and a face in its bulk spans six -- so a single data fault lights three detectors, the model is not graphlike, and the matching decoder refuses the patch exactly as it refuses the Steane model. That refusal is the decoder's property and not the patch's: the belief-propagation decoder answers the same model, and the patch's decoding evidence is recorded under that decoder's capability rather than this one's, because decoding reads a detector error model and not a code. The toric family has since landed on the same derivation route, and it is the first record here whose matrices leave more than one logical qubit: toric_code identifies the opposite sides of a square grid, so no check is cut down, the linear size is the distance the build must prove, and a default Z-basis memory experiment declares two observables rather than one, which is a change in the shape of the layout rather than in the contents of a row. The same family shows that graphlikeness can be a property of the noise declaration rather than of the code: a single-round model is graphlike under any noise because an X-type check has no interior round to separate a Y fault across, while at two rounds and more the two halves of that fault land on different round boundaries and the matcher refuses a model it accepted one round earlier. Both sides are measured at one code, round count and fault rate rather than recorded as a refusal alone. So the record set is eight families, two of them self-dual, while the families the CUDA-Q preview catalog names that still have no record here are absent for reasons that were measured rather than assumed. Its ReedMuller15 has since landed as a family of its own, and it is the first record here stated on the Boolean cube rather than on a lattice or on a group and the first whose two family distances are not equal: reed_muller_code punctures the two blocks two degrees apart at the one point naming every variable and takes their duals as the two check families, so a width-four cube returns the fifteen-qubit record with an X distance of seven beside a Z distance of three. Which block states which check family is a convention rather than a fact about the code, and this row states it rather than leaving a reader to infer it from two numbers: exchanging the two blocks is the same code with the two Pauli families renamed, which was measured by rounding both readings through qldpc_code before the rule was written, and the mirrored reading is the one that does not reproduce the sentence this row used to carry. The default bound of three therefore still refuses that code, and it refuses it because three is not a search over the X-type family rather than because the code's distance is not three; a bound of seven returns (7, 3) and a distance of three, and the record states both family distances separately rather than only their smaller. That bound is also the family's cost and the reason this route stops where it does: proving the X-type family's least operator has weight seven means exhausting every subset of weight up to six, which is 942648 subsets over the thirty-one points of width five, 75611760 over the sixty-three of width six and 5434287328 over the hundred and twenty-seven of width seven, each measured. Width four is the smallest cube whose punctured pair states a code at all -- at width three the two duals carry three and six rows over seven points and ten of those eighteen pairs of rows anticommute, so there is no stabilizer group to return -- and width five is the size the family is worth knowing for, thirty-one data qubits carrying eleven logical qubits three errors apart where a lattice patch of the same length carries one. Its zxxz_surface has since landed as the first record here whose checks are all mixed: flagquantum.qec.ZxxzSurfaceCode takes the rotated patch of the same distance and conjugates its checks by a Hadamard on the data checkerboard, so it occupies the rotated patch's own wires, declares the same ancillas in the same lattice order, has the same check weights and the same distance, and states the same stabilizer group up to a local Clifford -- while every one of its checks carries both factors and none is pure, which is why the matrix route cannot state it and the memory-circuit route can. Its logical pair is the two diagonals, declared Z first so the default Z-basis experiment reads the anti-diagonal, and which sublattice carries the Hadamards is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the other parity leaves that observable's coset with no pure-Z member at all, which is measured rather than argued. Running it also found the limit this row now records. A mixed check's outcome is deterministic neither at the all-zero preparation nor at a Z-basis readout, so no check of the Z-basis experiment is anchored in either place, and the experiment therefore carries detectors only between syndrome rounds and none at all from a syndrome round to the data. The consequence is a mechanism at every distance that fires no detector and flips the observable -- the readout, merging the logical operator's d wires into one mechanism of probability (1 - (1 - 2p) ** d) / 2 -- whose probability grows with the distance and which no pairing decoder can suppress, because there is no detector to pair. The matching decoder reproduces every syndrome it is handed on this code and still leaves the decoded rate above raw / 1.5 at distances three and five, against raw / 4 or better for the rotated patch through the identical harness, which is why this row records a limitation rather than a decoding result and why the ZXXZ patch is not yet a distance-d memory experiment in the sense the rotated patch's is. Its Tesseract is a subsystem code carrying gauge operators and a dressed distance, and no record here has a gauge subsystem at all. Its BareQubit does reach the record, so the trivial code is expressible without a family object. The qLDPC half of that pair has since landed, and it is the first record here that derives its logical operators as well as its matrices. bivariate_bicycle_code builds the bivariate-bicycle family from two polynomials over two cyclic coordinates, one check of each family per group element, so a check's weight is bounded by its polynomial's terms rather than by the periods; the logical operators are read out of the matrices as a null space modulo the stabilizer span, which is why flagquantum/qec/gf2.py gained that elimination rather than the family carrying a second copy of one, and each family comes back in the order the symplectic pairing puts it so lz[i] and lx[i] are partners rather than merely paired. Two numbers are the row's evidence. The logical count is the matrices' rank rather than their row count, so a construction that subtracted checks would report no logical qubit at all and refuse the smallest instance; and over Z_6 * Z_6 with A = x^3 + y + y^2 and B = y^3 + x + x^2 the record reports [[72, 12, 6]], the parameters the literature states for that pair, found by a search that ran about eighteen seconds against no measurable time for the eighteen-qubit member of the same family. The name that was still absent has since arrived: qldpc_code takes an arbitrary parity-check matrix pair and returns the record those matrices define, with the logical operators derived rather than asked for, so the reading the bicycle family needed for its own pair is now reachable directly and is stated once. It moved rather than doubled -- flagquantum/qec/qldpc.py owns the null space taken modulo the stabilizer span and the symplectic elimination after it, and the family calls those two helpers instead of carrying a second copy of them -- and before it was added it was held to four codes whose logical operators are declared elsewhere, with each derived operator required to differ from its declared partner by a check of its own type rather than merely agreeing with it on the count and the distance, because a complement of the stabilizer span is not unique. Two of its properties are why it is a route rather than a family. The logical count is the matrices' rank and not their row count, so a check written twice adds an ancilla and no logical qubit. And the distance is searched over the code rather than read off the derived operators, so the distance-three torus reports three while one of its derived Z-type operators spans seven data qubits. What remains absent on this row is now only two families: Reichardt and Floquet codes have neither a record nor a matrix route. The code records themselves still expose no decode entry point, because decoding belongs to the decoder row and reads a detector error model rather than a code. The noise record states a rate per fault family and the same rate per element, so a per-location profile is expressible: the four scalars and their per-qubit and per-check overrides are PhenomenologicalNoise's, read against the code's own vectors.
- `qec_decoder_family` (quantum_error_correction): Matching is now self-implemented rather than absent: the detector error model becomes a weighted decoding graph whose edge weight is log((1 - p) / p), and a syndrome is decoded exactly by enumerating the ways to pair its defective detectors and to route any of them to the graph's boundary. The row stays partial on scope, not on correctness. Matching needs a graphlike model and refuses a hyperedge rather than projecting it onto a pair, so a code whose mechanisms flip three or more detectors is outside this row's matching half. The pairing is enumerated, so a syndrome is bounded by a defect budget instead of decoded at scale. Belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding has since landed as flagquantum.qec.BeliefPropagationOsdDecoder, which answers a hyperedge model this row's matching half refuses, and it is recorded as a capability of its own rather than folded into this row's; and the registry landed with that decoder, so the matcher, the cross-check and the windowed matcher are reached by name while the hyperedge decoder is constructed directly, because a model carrying a three-detector mechanism has no pair-graph for the registry's protocol to promise. The sliding-window half has landed last and it is the authority over a window rather than a third opinion about a syndrome: flagquantum.qec.SlidingWindowMatchingDecoder cuts the detectors into bands advancing by `commit`, matches each window with this row's matcher, and commits the mechanisms whose first endpoint the band holds, so the defect budget bounds a window's syndrome instead of a whole history's. That is what answers the history an experiment produces: at a band of one span and a window of two it decoded every one of forty shots on histories of 122, 164, 480 and 1600 detectors where the exact matcher declined 11, 25, 40 and 40 of them. It is a replacement for the matcher rather than a second implementation beside it, and that is measured instead of argued: with one window covering the whole graph it returns the matcher's own mechanisms, observables and weight on every syndrome of a 200-shot history of the distance-three repetition and rotated surface codes. The window has a floor the constructor refuses by name, `window >= commit + span` for the model's measured widest mechanism, because a narrower window would commit a mechanism whose far endpoint it had rewritten as a step to the model's boundary. What the row still does not claim is an accuracy the narrow window does not have: over five short codes and 400 shots each the disagreements with the exact matcher's observables fell from 0, 1, 2, 7 and 12 at a window of two bands to 0, 0, 0, 0 and 4 at four bands while the widest code refused one shot of its 400 at five bands, so agreement is bought with the width rather than guaranteed and is not monotone in it, and no threshold and no logical error rate is estimated from a windowed decode. There is also no streaming entry point and no chunk seam to feed one, which is the DEM-chunking row rather than this one. The baseline's GPU decoders are deliberately not chased, because the CUDA-Q qLDPC decoder is a closed-source shared library, so only its interface position is a target and an Apache-2.0 implementation is the route if that scope is ever reached. The row fails closed on a second gap of its own: because the graph keeps one edge per mechanism, a model that states one detector-and-observable signature twice would become two parallel edges and the matcher would take the cheaper, so the decoder requires a unique signature before it weights anything and refuses a duplicate with the merge that resolves it named in the refusal. It fails closed on the neighbouring statement for the neighbouring reason: a model that says two mechanisms are alternatives is refused and the groups are named, because one weight per mechanism is the weight of a fault that fires alone while a group of alternatives is one fault whose weight is the negative log-likelihood of the group, so weighting the members separately would charge the model more than the fault costs. The cross-check half has landed and it is a comparison of two selections rather than an equality of two instruments: PyMatching is behind the `pymatching` extra and is never the authority, and because its own accumulator reports 3.9020747171643912 for a mechanism this row states as 3.9020746947749574 the graph it minimizes over is not exactly this one. The row therefore asserts the cheapest weight on every syndrome, the observables wherever the cheapest explanation is unique, and the two refusals as the same set, with a pinned tie on the distance-three repetition code so the tie clause is demonstrated. The registry, the decoder families the matcher does not cover, and the hyperedge front end were the work this row still named; of those, the hyperedge decoder has landed as described above, and the registry has landed as the factory half of the baseline's decoder surface rather than the whole of it: flagquantum.qec.get_decoder(name, source, **options) reaches a decoder by name and flagquantum.qec.register_decoder(name, *, replace=False) puts one there, with registration checked while the registering module is imported so a class missing decode or from_detector_error_model is refused there rather than at the first caller. The registry is deliberately narrower than upstream's. Its source argument takes the three carriers a caller can hold a model in -- the detector error model, stim's text for one, and the decoding graph the model defines -- and not H_or_dem_text_or_sparse_matrix, because lifting a parity-check matrix would also mean choosing the noise model and round count that from_code_matrices reads rather than defaults. It holds the detector-error-model family alone, because the repetition-code decoders here take an ordered syndrome history rather than detection events and one name space over two input protocols would make a name mean one of two things. It fails closed rather than falling back: an unregistered name raises and lists the registered names, a source that is not one of the three carriers is refused by type, and no name is preferred over another, so the authority is returned for its own name wherever the optional extra happens to be installed. The remaining work inside this row is therefore the plugin boundary the baseline ships, whatever would make a hyperedge decoder nameable, and a streaming decode over a chunk seam this package does not have -- the registered adapter is a concrete class under a name rather than a plugin loaded across a version boundary, and the hyperedge decoder is reachable from the package but not through the registry.
- `qec_stim_integration` (quantum_error_correction): All three halves now exist, and the row is partial on scope rather than on connection. Stim-backed sampling landed with the stabilizer engine, the detector error model half landed with the text reader and its own capability entry, and the join landed last: a memory circuit is lowered once, each configured noise location is placed at the instruction it belongs to, the result is executed on the stabilizer engine, and the detection events and observable flips are read off the recorded bits. A decoder built from that same circuit's model then decodes those events, so a logical-failure rate no longer needs the statevector ceiling that bounds construction. What the row still lacks is breadth of the noise grammar: a location is a data flip at a round boundary or a measurement flip at a check's readout, which is what the phenomenological record names, while a channel placed after an arbitrary gate has no location and is still declined. The x_ and z_ variants are absent for the same reason the code record is a Z-memory record. Decoding itself stays with the decoder row rather than being implied here. The row names three registry entries because the implementation genuinely spans three: the sampling half is `stabilizer_sampling`, the interchange half is `detector_error_model`, and the join that consumes both is `qec_memory_circuit_sampling`. The row is read only against cudaq-qec, which is where the detector error models live; where the two components divide this surface is recorded in `baseline.surface_ownership`.
- `third_party_target_sdk` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Partial. A third party declares its device in an extension manifest, FlagQuantum validates the declaration fail-closed into a capability snapshot, and `flagquantum.remote.emulation.emulate_declared_target` turns one validated declaration into the target profile the existing emulation entry already executes: the declared capacity, native gates, connectivity, result formats, and shot and operation limits are the device's own statements, and the compiled program is routed, legalized, emitted, re-parsed, and run locally with the caller's noise model or the device's own calibration. What is absent is a run on the provider's own hardware: execution through a declaration is local emulation of the declared device, and reaching the device itself still needs a provider adapter under the existing provider contract.
- `provider_roster_breadth` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Partial. IonQ, Quantinuum, IQM, and neutral-atom declarations are read fail-closed into backend profiles, preflighted locally, and driven through the existing `remote/qpu` provider contract, alongside the existing Quafu, Braket, and Azure adapters. Still absent: photonic and quantum-control-system providers, an analog-schedule submission path for neutral atoms, and any hardware evidence, because no adapter has been exercised against a live provider.
- `simulator_plugin_admission` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): The crossing is landed and exercised; the gap is that nothing installed stands on it. `flagquantum/ecosystem/extensions/admission.py` imports `flagquantum.runtime.backend_registry` and registers one route through the existing `register_backend`, so an extension backend discovered from the `flagquantum.extensions` entry-point group does execute: a third-party backend written against the public extension namespace alone runs through `fq.run`, and a run on it reports `execution_path = admitted_extension_backend` with a state that matches the built-in engine. What the distribution declares is one entry point, `backend.qiskit_aer`, and it predates the route contract: its `execute(program, parameters=None)` is the SDK member rather than the Runtime route, and because both protocols are `runtime_checkable` it passes both `isinstance` checks. Admission now binds the declared call and refuses it by name, so this row is a capability with no conforming occupant rather than a protocol with no crossing, and the refusal is the honest state: a backend that cannot be called as `execute(program, *, options)` is rejected before a plan exists instead of failing inside a planned execution. NVQIR's ABI half is a separate row. The audit checked the token's own phrase against the registry rather than against the tree, because the two say different things. capability-maturity.toml's `extension_sdk` row states that there is no stable C ABI, no out-of-process backend, no per-execution discovery, and no numerical equivalence certification between an admitted backend and the built-in engine, and that row's own `focused_tests` is tests/unit/test_backend_execution_admission.py -- the file whose `test_the_reference_backend_agrees_with_the_builtin_engine` runs all ten declared gates, three controls among them with control above target, and asserts the admitted state against a plain run of the same circuit to 1e-5. So a measurement exists and a certification does not, and the token is a quotation of the second statement rather than a denial of the first. Nothing in admission itself compares numerals: it establishes the protocol member and the call shape, so a backend is admitted on shape and on its negotiated capabilities and its agreement with the built-in engine is not a condition of admission.
- `large_scale_statevector` (performance_and_scalability): The measured FlagQuantum point is a 32-qubit complex128 forward pass on one eight-accelerator node, which is a development-evidence result and is not comparable to the baseline scale. No row here is a performance claim.
- `production_sharded_statevector` (performance_and_scalability): The registered level is below production, so the sharded path cannot support a capacity-expansion claim yet.

**next** (34 open)

- `runtime_qubit_allocation` (language_and_programming_model): Wire count is fixed at circuit construction. Runtime allocation is designed in the QuantumIR level and is not implemented.
- `pauli_tracking_sbe` (language_and_programming_model): Both halves of the name are now implemented for Pauli inputs. A frame is tracked through a noise instruction rather than refused, on as many wires as the channel acts on, so a noisy Clifford program is sampled without a dense state; and a measurement is expanded in a stabilizer basis by `pauli_readout`, which conjugates a Pauli string through the whole program, reports the conjugated string and its power of `i`, and reads the exact expectation of one of `-1`, `0`, `1` against the state the circuit starts from. The expansion is first-party integer bookkeeping and imports no distribution, so the two halves no longer share a dependency. A general channel is still refused instead of being sampled as its nearest Pauli approximation, so the non-Pauli branch the name implies is absent rather than approximated. Detection events are not emitted, and observable flips are reported as a conjugated string rather than as a per-shot flip record.
- `global_seed_control` (language_and_programming_model): Seeding is per call rather than process wide. `ExecutionOptions` carries a seed and the training path carries its own seeder, so a user reproduces a run by threading a seed through each entry point instead of stating one seed for the session. The audit measured that absence: no `seed` and no `set_seed` appears in `flagquantum.__all__`, which holds 36 names, and no module-level `def seed` or `def set_seed` exists anywhere under flagquantum/. What the tree offers instead are per-call arguments, such as the `seed` keyword of the stabilizer executor route and the `torch.Generator` seeded per call in flagquantum/runtime/dynamic/execution.py.
- `gate_decomposition_patterns` (compiler_and_ir): `flagquantum/compiler/basis_translation.py` carries a rule library of 18 documented identities over the 31 declared unitary opcodes, and the coverage it buys is measured rather than claimed: `tests/unit/test_decomposition_pattern_coverage.py` converts every declared unitary opcode into two named bases and sorts each outcome into the kind of refusal that produced it. Into Clifford+T the library reaches ten opcodes and refuses twenty-one, and the twenty-one are two different failures. Eleven carry a rule whose own leaves ask for a gate the basis does not publish, so the rewrite stops on the escaped leaf and the refusal names that leaf; the other ten have no rule at all. A rule is therefore necessary and not sufficient, and a coverage number read off the table alone overstates what a tight basis reaches by exactly those eleven opcodes. Into a basis publishing a z-rotation and a two-wire entangler all 31 convert, including the thirteen no rule names, because the Euler and KAK syntheses reach what the table does not, and every one of those conversions is compared against its source through the runtime's statevector kernel up to one global phase. What the row is still missing is the library's shape rather than its width: the rules are Python builder functions in one mapping instead of a declarative pattern a caller can inspect, compose, or load as data, and a registered identity carries no name, version, or provenance of its own.
- `basis_conversion` (compiler_and_ir): A program converts into any named basis the caller writes down, and every rewrite is exact: a gate outside the basis with no verified decomposition is refused by name, a decomposition whose own leaves escape the basis is refused by name, and the four refusal kinds are enumerated in REFUSAL_KINDS. The identity table is extensible through with_equivalence_rule, which validates a rule and returns a new frozen mapping rather than editing the shared one, so a caller holding a verified identity the table does not name can register it without a second registry and without changing what any other caller sees.
- `clifford_t_synthesis` (compiler_and_ir): The exact quarter-turn slice exists. Every rz, phase, or u1 rotation whose angle is an exact multiple of pi/4 is classified by residue modulo eight and rewritten into a table word over t, tdg, s, sdg, and z, so a target publishing only h, s, t, and cx now reaches a rotation it previously refused; each residue carries a shortest word and a fallback that keeps it reachable when the target omits one of an inverse pair, and a test enumerates the vocabulary to re-derive the shortest-word claim rather than trusting the table. Approximating an arbitrary angle is absent and is a different problem: the Ross-Selinger route needs exact arithmetic in Z[omega, 1/sqrt(2)], a Diophantine norm equation, and integer factorization, none of which FlagQuantum carries.
- `angle_synthesis` (compiler_and_ir): The exact half exists and is shared with the row above: a rotation is recognized as a quarter turn by an exact comparison against n * (pi/4) and answered with a word naming only plain named gates, and the recognition refuses a trainable angle so a rotation never leaves the autograd graph. Accuracy-directed approximation is absent: no target accuracy is accepted, no epsilon is spent, and the GMP and MPFR route the strategy document records for it is not adopted. The audit measured where tolerances do live, because what is absent is the accuracy argument rather than tolerance itself: _UNITARY_ATOL = 1.0e-9 in flagquantum/compiler/one_qubit_synthesis.py and again in two_qubit_synthesis.py beside _M2_ATOL = 1.0e-13, which decides whether a 2x2 matrix counts as unitary at all, and the only tolerance-valued parameter in the package is the private _is_zero(value, atol=1e-12) in flagquantum/compiler/pipeline.py, which answers whether a raised quantity is zero rather than how close a rotation is to its target. A caller asking for a rotation to within 1e-10 is still refused, and refused because no entry point takes the number.
- `commutation_aware_rewrite` (compiler_and_ir): The analysis and one rewrite consumer are implemented. `flagquantum/compiler/commutation.py` answers the two questions a reduction needs -- whether two instructions commute, and which instructions form one commuting block on a wire -- and its rule source is a source of proof rather than of record: it reads the two instructions' operator schemas and proves the commutation, with disjoint support unconditional and a gate the rule source has no rule for treated as a barrier. `flagquantum/compiler/commutation_cancellation.py` is the consumer: `cancel_commuting_self_inverse` removes parameter-free, matrix-free members of the self-inverse set in proven pairs, keeping the last member of an odd group so what the block preserves is applied as late as it was before, and it is scheduled inside the pipeline's fixed-point loop, so `cx(0, 1) rz(0) cx(0, 1)` reduces to `rz(0)` where the wire-local self-inverse merge could not see it. What is absent is the part CUDA-Q's row is named for. CUDA-Q's pass is a driver: `CommutationAwareRewriteMatcher` searches backward from an anchor operation for the nearest earlier endpoint that a consumer will accept, crossing a frontier only where pairwise commutation or disjoint support is proven, and the consumer owns the endpoint's algebraic identity. FlagQuantum has one consumer hard-coded against the analysis instead of a matcher a second rewrite can plug into, so no pass can reorder a gate past a commuter to expose a cancellation that a different pass then takes. There is also no linear-use-def guard, because `CircuitIR` is a straight-line instruction list in which nothing can branch -- the same fact that makes the guard unnecessary here is what makes the search unnecessary, so the guard and the search are one gap rather than two. The audit corrected the invalidation half against the tree rather than against the reason this row carried. `flagquantum/compiler/pass_manager.py` exists and carries the machinery: `PassSpec` at `:178` declares `uses` and `preserves` at `:190`, and `resolve_sequence` refuses a pass that claims to preserve an analysis that is a function of the program, because a transformation may return a different program (`:446`) -- so the program-derived `commutation_blocks` is exactly the analysis that cannot be vouched for and is therefore recomputed, while the program-independent `self_inverse_opcodes` is carried. `flagquantum/compiler/pipeline.py:408` is where that is declared for the pass this row already reports: `cancel_commuting_self_inverse` reads both analyses and preserves only `self_inverse_opcodes`. The two refusals are pinned by `tests/unit/test_compiler_pass_manager.py:578` and `:591`, and the registration of `commutation_blocks` as an `AnalysisSpec` is pinned by `tests/unit/test_compilation_commutation_cancellation.py:445`. So per-block invalidation is present, and what is absent is only the driver: the neighbouring guard goes with its own precondition, because a straight-line `CircuitIR` cannot branch and needs no linear-use-def guard.
- `dead_code_elimination` (compiler_and_ir): Absent, and the earlier reason this row gave -- that it depends on the pass infrastructure -- does not survive measurement, because that infrastructure now exists and the row is still absent. The premise the earlier reason leaned on -- that the neighbouring commutation row was reconciled without any pass infrastructure at all -- is corrected here, because that row's per-block analysis invalidation is supplied by exactly such infrastructure: `flagquantum/compiler/pass_manager.py` is a named pass registry with declared analyses and `flagquantum/compiler/pipeline.py` consumes it. The dependency this row once named is therefore satisfied rather than pending, which makes the row's own conclusion stronger rather than weaker: what blocks it is the output-class semantics, which no amount of pass machinery answers. CUDA-Q's pass does two things, and neither has a representation here. It removes a `quake.null_wire` whose only use is `quake.sink`, and a `quake.alloca` whose only use is its matching `quake.dealloc` or which has no use at all. `CircuitIR` declares its width once as `n_wires` and the operator schema table holds no allocation, release, null-wire, or sink opcode, so a wire that was never allocated cannot exist and the object this elimination removes is not denotable. What is left is the general half -- a gate whose result no later reader observes -- and that is where the semantics first have to be settled, because the answer differs by output class. `fq.run` returns the whole statevector, so a gate on a wire nothing else touches is observable in the returned state and eliminating it would change the result; a program that declares `measurements` or `observables` has named its outputs, and only there can a wire with no reader be dead. A pass written against one reading would be wrong for the other, and no such declaration of output class is a property of `CircuitIR` today: an empty measurements tuple means both `the caller wants no measurement` and `the state is the answer`. That distinction is the work this row is actually waiting on, and it is recorded rather than implied.
- `target_text_emitters` (compiler_and_ir): An OpenQASM emitter exists. The emitter set is narrower than the CUDA-Q roster.
- `resource_estimation` (compiler_and_ir): The static half exists. `flagquantum/compiler/resource_estimation.py` reports the operation count per opcode, the schedule depth, the per-wire depth, the widest operation, the T family and its depth, the channel count, and the declared register width, over the counted instruction sequence, with the basis named in the record as `static_instruction_sequence` for a program counted as written or as a `named_basis:` label for one counted after conversion. Calling it with `gates` converts the program first, so the figure a caller wants is available even when the program is not written in it -- a quarter-turn rotation is one `rz` as written and one `t` under a named basis, and a compound gate acquires the T-count of the decomposition the built-in table gives it. It refuses a program whose sequence has data dependence, naming the instruction index, and that refusal is what the row now turns on: a straight-line list has no loop bound, so loops and functions stay unestimatable. The cause this row first gave is narrower than it read: no symbol named `ProgramIR` occurs in any Python module under `flagquantum/`, `tests/`, `examples/` or `tools/`, while a program-level IR does exist privately -- `flagquantum/compiler/_hybrid/model.py:203` is a typed container with blocks and regions, and it declares itself a single-function one -- so what the estimator waits on is a program-level IR it can read rather than any program IR at all. This one prices a `CircuitIR` or any object exposing `to_ir()`, and the private container exposes `to_data()` instead, which is why a loop bound could not be handed to it even if one existed, exactly as this row recorded before any of the rest was built. The estimate is also not a latency and not a device cost -- no gate duration, connectivity, or routing overhead enters it -- and the conversion a named basis triggers is a rewrite, not a run: it raises the same refusal `convert_basis` raises when the basis cannot express the program exactly, so no count is ever of an approximate sequence. The conversion's identity travels on the record, so a count over a rewritten sequence is traceable to the rewrite that produced it. Qubit peak is not a separate field; the register width and the used wires are. The fault-tolerant layer above the tally landed separately, as `flagquantum.algorithms.logical_resources` charging the tally on a rotated surface code.

The OpenQASM half is the inverse of the emitter over one canonical subset rather than a general front end: the names it accepts in a version lane are exactly the names the emitter writes in that lane, 25 of the 28 declared spellings in OpenQASM 2 and 24 in OpenQASM 3, and the difference between the lanes is the spelling each one canonically writes rather than a gap in either.
